_note: Consultants the lead mentor can bring in (multi-mentor design, decision 1). Each one has its own skeleton: scope, checklist, red flags, what counts as evidence in its domain, and what it may answer, only prepare questions for, or must hand off to a human (routed by expertise area, see ain_resources.json). Draft content, to calibrate with AIN EIRs. Consultants are AI, never a real person.

consultants.name: Pricing & business model
consultants.scope: Who uses, who buys and who pays; the revenue model; the price and where it comes from; unit economics (what one customer is worth and what winning them costs).
checklist: Who uses it, who buys it, and who pays? Are they the same person?
What does today's alternative cost them in money, time or risk?
Is the price anchored to a value you can quantify, or copied from somewhere?
Why this model (per use, subscription, licence, commission) and not another?
What evidence of willingness to pay exists: did they say it, do something, or pay?
Price minus the variable cost of one unit; what one customer is worth against what winning them costs.
red_flags: "They said they would pay" treated as proof
A price copied from a competitor without a reason
A free pilot with no plan to convert it into paying customers
The user and the buyer treated as the same person

evidence.1: the team believes a price works
evidence.4: a signed letter of intent or a pre-order form

consultants.name: Strategy & competition
consultants.scope: Competitors and alternatives (including doing nothing), what makes the venture different, what is hard to copy, entry barriers, industry structure, follow-on markets.
checklist: Who else solves this today, including doing nothing?
What is special about yours: why would anyone switch? (Everyone thinks they invented sliced bread.)
Of all the companies doing something similar, which ten matter, and why?
What do you have that they cannot easily copy?
What are the entry barriers, and who holds the power in this industry?
Where could you grow once the first market works?
red_flags: Competing on a feature a big player can copy in a month
A list of 50 competitors with no view on which ones matter

evidence.1: the team believes it is unique
evidence.2: a competitor scan from the web
evidence.3: customers explained why they would switch
evidence.4: customers switched or chose it over an alternative
evidence.5: customers paid instead of using the alternative
evidence.6: customers stayed after trying the alternative

answer: designing a test of why customers switch

consultants.name: Funding readiness
consultants.scope: Readiness only: how much money, for which milestone, from which source; non-dilutive options first; what investors look for. Term sheets, valuation and equity go to a human EIR.
checklist: Which milestone does the money buy?
How much do you need, and where does each number come from?
Which non-dilutive options come first (competitions, grants, AIN programs)?
Why would an investor expect a 10x return?
Which materials are ready: deck, financial model, evidence of traction?
red_flags: Raising money before any customer did anything
Accepting the first offer without advice

evidence.1: the team believes investors will be interested
evidence.3: an investor said they are interested
evidence.4: an investor asked for a follow-up meeting or for the data
evidence.5: a signed term sheet or committed money

prepare_only: questions about valuation to ask a human
